financials_interim.notes: Source: CSE auto-discovered doc source_id 52497 (path 723_1786618662400.pdf), Maskeliya Plantations PLC 'Interim Financial Statements ... For the three months ended 30 June 2026', authorized for issue 12 Aug 2026. Single-entity filing -> one GROUP row. Page cites per the PDF's own page footer ('( 0N )'): P&L p.2, SOFP p.4, Statement of Changes in Equity p.5, Cash Flow p.6, Notes p.7, Segment Information (by estate) p.8. EXTRACTION QUALITY: this PDF's default text layer is severely column-corrupted (numeric cells frequently land on the wrong printed row, e.g. an early naive read showed Management Fee and Finance Cost swapped between years). All figures here come from pdfplumber's layout-preserving re-extraction and are independently verified: (1) Segment Information's Total Segments Gross Profit (292,361/321,857 for 2026/2025) plus Other income minus Admin expenses minus Management fee minus Finance cost reconciles exactly to the printed PBT (197,048/233,137) for both years; (2) SOFP Non-Current Assets components (507,921+928,665+2,308,878+1,485,147+0=5,230,611) and Current Assets components (19,628+1,454,297+674,460+59,985+55,044=2,263,414) both sum to their printed subtotals, and 5,230,611+2,263,414=7,494,025 matches printed Total Assets; (3) Total Equity (3,122,550) is independently confirmed via the Statement of Changes in Equity roll-forward (673,721 Stated Capital + 540,000 General Reserve + 449,523 Retained Earnings + 1,459,306 Timber Reserve) and via Net Assets Per Share (Rs.57.87) x 53,953,490 shares = Rs.3,122,340k, consistent within rounding; (4) Total Liabilities = Non-Current (2,892,129) + Current (1,479,346) = 4,371,475 = Total Assets - Total Equity, closes exactly. EPS cross-check: PAT 154,618k / 53,953,490 shares = Rs.2.866/share, matches printed Rs.2.87. Operating_profit has no printed subtotal (P&L goes straight from Gross Profit/Other Income/Admin/Mgmt Fee to Finance Cost then PBT) -- derived as Gross profit + Other income - Administrative expenses - Management fee = Rs.292,361+55-28,559-35,498=Rs.228,359k (this is PBT before Finance Cost only, i.e. Rs.228,359-31,311=197,048=PBT, consistent). No separate 'Finance Income' line exists in MASK's P&L (only Finance Cost is shown) -- finance_income left unset rather than assumed zero, since the Cash Flow Statement does show a small separate 'Finance Income' cash-received line (Rs.408k) suggesting a non-P&L-line financing income exists but isn't broken out in the income statement. Within Non-Current Liabilities, 'Interest Bearing Loans & Borrowings' is printed as nil/nil and 'Retiring Benefit Obligations' as Rs.1,333,842k/1,325,064k (30.06.2026/31.03.2026) -- taken literally as printed (a very large gratuity provision is plausible for a century-old estate workforce); long_term_borrowings is therefore set to 0, and all of MASK's Rs.370,827k interest-bearing debt is short-term. No wage/labour-cost or government-wage-revision commentary is disclosed anywhere in this filing (genuine gap, flagged in interim_updates.gaps_note); MASK's principal business is described as 'Cultivation, Manufacture and Sale of Tea, Planting and sale of Timber' only -- there is no tea/rubber/other crop-mix segmentation to report (MASK is a single-crop, four-estate plantation company; its segment note is by estate, not by crop).

interim_updates.note_text: Maskeliya Plantations PLC (MASK) reported Revenue of Rs.1,659,054k for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), -2.5% YoY (2025: Rs.1,702,388k), Profit Before Taxation of Rs.197,048k, -15.5% YoY (2025: Rs.233,137k), and Net Profit of Rs.154,618k, -11.8% YoY (2025: Rs.175,031k). MASK's principal business is Tea cultivation plus Timber sales only (no rubber/other crop mix); its Segment Information note (p.8) instead breaks results out by estate. Of the four estates, Bandarawela drove the bulk of the decline: its Gross Profit fell 52.4% YoY to Rs.35,416k (2025: Rs.74,377k, -Rs.38,961k) even though its revenue fell only 3.3% (Rs.376,786k vs Rs.389,716k) -- Bandarawela's revenue-expenditure ratio deteriorated sharply from 76.9% of segment revenue (Rs.299,520k/Rs.389,716k) to 85.4% (Rs.321,809k/Rs.376,786k), a c.850bps cost-ratio deterioration, the largest of any estate. Upcot also weakened, Gross Profit -17.6% to Rs.71,490k (2025: Rs.86,711k) on a 4.7% revenue decline. These two were partially offset by Talawakelle, whose Gross Profit rose 28.9% to Rs.96,238k (2025: Rs.74,647k, +Rs.21,591k) despite revenue growing only 0.6% -- implying a meaningful cost improvement at that estate specifically. Maskeliya estate was broadly flat (Gross Profit +3.6% to Rs.89,217k). Combined, the four estates' Total Segment Gross Profit fell 9.2% YoY to Rs.292,361k (2025: Rs.321,857k, -Rs.29,496k), with Bandarawela's Rs.38,961k decline more than accounting for the whole Group shortfall before Talawakelle's offsetting improvement. Below Gross Profit, Other Income collapsed 98.8% YoY to just Rs.55k (2025: Rs.4,522k), Administration Expenses rose 17.1% to Rs.28,559k (2025: Rs.24,382k), and Finance Cost rose 13.2% to Rs.31,311k (2025: Rs.27,662k) -- consistent with new short-term interest-bearing borrowings of Rs.370,827k at 30 June 2026 versus none at 31 March 2026. These were partially cushioned by a 13.8% fall in Management Fee to Rs.35,498k (2025: Rs.41,198k). Net Profit's decline (-11.8%) was less severe than PBT's (-15.5%) because the effective tax rate fell to 21.5% (Rs.42,430k/Rs.197,048k) from 24.9% (Rs.58,106k/Rs.233,137k) YoY, unexplained in the filing. Operating cash flow swung sharply negative, Net Cash from Operating Activities of Rs.(350,539)k versus Rs.36,063k in the prior-year quarter, driven mainly by a Rs.475,285k build in Inventories (2025: only Rs.185,922k) -- a working-capital, not profitability, story, but worth flagging given the scale of the swing.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is MASK's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter previously stored; the prior manual document registered for MASK, source_id manual_b6f790edd2b8dcac, covered the quarter ended 30 Sep 2024 and was superseded by this fresher quarter-ended-30-June-2026 filing, source_id 52497). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no wage/labour-cost or government minimum-wage-revision commentary is disclosed anywhere in this filing, despite plantation labour being the likely driver of Bandarawela's c.850bps cost-ratio deterioration -- the filing gives no estate-specific narrative explanation, only the segment numbers; (2) the c.340bps YoY fall in effective tax rate (24.9% to 21.5%) is not explained; (3) Non-Current Liabilities show 'Retiring Benefit Obligations' of Rs.1,333,842k (30.06.2026) / Rs.1,325,064k (31.03.2026), a very large provision relative to the company's size, taken as printed but not independently verified against the Annual Report; (4) the Rs.475,285k Q1 inventory build driving the operating cash outflow is not narratively explained (could be seasonal made-tea/timber stock buildup ahead of sales, but not stated); (5) this PDF's default text layer suffered severe column-order corruption; all figures used here were independently cross-checked via pdfplumber's layout-preserving re-extraction and multiple arithmetic identities (PBT reconciliation, balance sheet subtotal sums, NAV/share back-solve, equity roll-forward), documented in financial_statements.notes.
interim_updates.takeaway: MASK's Q1 FY2026/27 profit decline (PBT -15.5%, PAT -11.8%) is not a broad-based Revenue story (Revenue fell only 2.5%) but is concentrated almost entirely in one estate -- Bandarawela, where a c.850bps cost-ratio deterioration halved Gross Profit -- partially cushioned by a strong improvement at Talawakelle. New short-term borrowings (Rs.370,827k, absent at the last financial year-end) are a fresh source of finance-cost pressure to watch going forward. None of the profitability swings are explained by wage or input-cost commentary in the filing itself, which is a genuine disclosure gap for a labour-intensive plantation business.

yoy.label: Operating profit (derived: Gross profit + Other income - Admin exp - Mgmt fee)

operational_highlights: By estate (Gross Profit): Bandarawela -52.4% YoY to Rs.35,416k (revenue-expenditure ratio worsened from 76.9% to 85.4% of its revenue, c.850bps); Upcot -17.6% to Rs.71,490k; Talawakelle +28.9% to Rs.96,238k; Maskeliya +3.6% to Rs.89,217k.

Total Segment Gross Profit -9.2% YoY to Rs.292,361k; Bandarawela's Rs.38,961k decline alone exceeded the Group's total Rs.29,496k Gross Profit shortfall, partly offset by Talawakelle's Rs.21,591k improvement.
Other Income collapsed 98.8% YoY to Rs.55k (2025: Rs.4,522k); Finance Cost +13.2% to Rs.31,311k as new short-term borrowings of Rs.370,827k appeared at 30 June 2026 (nil at 31 March 2026).
Effective tax rate fell to 21.5% from 24.9% YoY, cushioning Net Profit's decline (-11.8%) relative to PBT's (-15.5%).
Net Cash from Operating Activities swung to Rs.(350,539)k from +Rs.36,063k PY, driven by a Rs.475,285k Q1 inventory build.
key_drivers: Bandarawela estate Gross Profit collapse (-52.4% YoY, -Rs.38,961k) on a c.850bps revenue-expenditure-ratio deterioration (76.9% to 85.4% of its own revenue) is the single largest driver of the Group's profit decline -- larger by itself than the Group's entire Rs.29,496k Gross Profit shortfall.
Talawakelle estate's Gross Profit improvement (+28.9% YoY, +Rs.21,591k) on essentially flat revenue (+0.6%) partially offset Bandarawela and Upcot's declines.
New short-term interest-bearing borrowings (Rs.370,827k at 30 June 2026, nil at FYE) drove Finance Cost +13.2% YoY, adding a further drag below Gross Profit.
A c.340bps fall in the effective tax rate (24.9% to 21.5%, unexplained) let Net Profit decline less (-11.8%) than PBT (-15.5%).
